newsitem.title: USA: Nantucket Island awash in candy.
newsitem.headline: Nantucket Island awash in candy.

text.p: Beachcombers on Thursday picked through thousands of Hershey Kisses, Tootsie Rolls and other candies that washed up on Nantucket Island after a container ship lost its cargo in heavy winds.

The Polish-registered ship Pol America lost 23 cargo containers filled with everything from candy to shoes, furniture and a car when it encountered near-hurricane winds and waves as high as 30 feet (nine metres), U.S. Coast Guard Petty Officer Roger Weatherell told Reuters.
Most of the cargo apparently sank and the ship safely continued its journey to Baltimore, but the treats began washing up on the eastern shore of the Massachusetts vacation island.
"There's every choice of candy you could ever imagine washing up in the surf," Nantucket Police Chief Randolph Norris. "It's pretty much a mess."

Local residents turned out on Thursday to help clean up the debris. The endangered right whale spawns in the spring in Nantucket waters and locals feared the whales and other animals could choke on the candy.
Health officials warned islanders not to indulge.
"We've told everybody not to eat it unless the bags were intact," Weatherell said. "If they're sealed, it's okay."
